message:
Hello Emily Johnson, I am Noah, an AI interviewer.

This conversation will take about 20 minutes. The goal is to get a deep understanding of your work, your role, expertise, daily tasks, the tools you use, any challenges you face, and your ambitions for the future.
Before we begin, could you let me know in which language you would like to do this interview? You can choose Dutch, French, German, or English.
English is fine.

Perfect, we'll continue in English then.

Let me start by getting to know you better — could you tell me what your job title is and what your role involves?

I'm a Process Coordinator. My role involves optimizing and coordinating various processes to improve operational efficiency. I handle things like student ticket handling, complaint management, and incident resolution.
That sounds like you're quite central to keeping things running smoothly — can you walk me through what a typical day or week looks like for you in terms of your main tasks?

Sure, my days usually involve managing and coordinating the processes I oversee. I'll start by checking any new student tickets or complaints that have come in. From there, I coordinate with different teams to ensure each step in the process is followed correctly. I also handle any issues that come up, like incorrect ticket information or missing documents, and work on optimizing these processes to make them more efficient.
That's helpful — roughly how much time per day would you say you spend on checking and managing those incoming tickets and complaints?
I spend a good portion of my day on them, maybe around 60 to 90 minutes, depending on the volume we receive. It varies day by day.
And when you're coordinating with different teams to ensure processes are followed — how often does that happen and how long does it typically take?
I coordinate with different teams daily. It usually takes a few hours spread throughout the day, as I need to ensure everything moves smoothly from one step to the next.
Got it, so a few hours daily on coordination — that's significant time. What about the optimization work you mentioned, how frequently do you focus on improving those processes?
I try to fit in optimization work whenever I can, often a few times a week. It's more of an ongoing effort to tweak things as I notice inefficiencies.
Makes sense — so optimization is more sporadic. When you do spot those inefficiencies, what are the most common problems you find, and roughly how much time do you think gets wasted because of them?

Common problems include incorrect ticket information or missing reference documents, which cause delays. It's hard to say exactly how much time is wasted, but addressing these issues can definitely slow things down by a few hours or even a day in some cases.
That sounds frustrating — which of these issues happens most often, and what usually causes them in the first place?
Incorrect ticket information happens most often. It's usually caused by students not providing all the necessary details when they first open a ticket.
So incomplete information from the start creates rework — when that happens, how do you typically handle it, and how much back-and-forth does it usually involve?
I usually request the student to resubmit the correct information. It can involve a few emails back and forth, depending on how quickly they respond and provide the needed details.
I see — and beyond those ticket issues, what else frustrates you most about your day-to-day work or slows you down?
Sometimes, miscommunication about incident progress can be frustrating. When status updates aren't done correctly, it takes extra time to review logs and update them manually.
How often does that miscommunication happen, and roughly how much time per week would you say you spend fixing those manual updates?
It doesn't happen too often, maybe a couple of times a week. Fixing those manual updates can take around 30 minutes to an hour each time.
That adds up — so maybe an hour or two per week just on fixing those updates. What tools are you currently using to manage all of this work?

I use a variety of tools like Sipac for student tickets, a Complaint System for complaints, and an Incident Management System for incident resolution. Email and internal communication tools are also essential for coordinating with teams.
How do you feel about these tools — do they work well together, or do you find yourself switching between them constantly?
They work fairly well, but there is some switching involved. It would be nice if they were more integrated to reduce the back-and-forth.
What would better integration look like for you — what's the biggest pain point when switching between them?

Better integration would mean sharing information seamlessly between tools without needing to enter the same data multiple times. The biggest pain point is the manual entry and ensuring all systems reflect the latest updates.
That makes sense — so duplicate data entry is a real drain. Beyond the tools themselves, how well do you cooperate with other teams internally, and are there any bottlenecks there?
We generally cooperate well, but sometimes bottlenecks happen when a team is overloaded or if there's miscommunication. Keeping everyone on the same page can be challenging.
When those bottlenecks happen, how much does it typically impact your work — do you find yourself waiting around, or does it create extra tasks for you?
It can create extra tasks, like following up more frequently or trying to find workarounds. Sometimes there's a bit of waiting involved too, but I try to keep things moving as much as possible.
That's proactive of you — now, thinking about your role going forward, how do you see it evolving in the future, and what would you like to spend more time on?

I'd like to spend more time on process optimization and finding ways to streamline our workflows. As the role evolves, I hope to focus more on strategic improvements rather than just day-to-day coordination.
That's a clear vision — if you could wave a magic wand and fix one thing about your workflow right now, what would it be?
I'd integrate all our tools to minimize manual data entry and ensure everything is updated automatically across systems.
That's a powerful one — beyond automation, what are your broader ambitions for your career or this role over the next year or two?
I'd like to take on more responsibility in process design and optimization, potentially leading initiatives to implement more efficient systems company-wide.

That's ambitious and aligns well with what you're already doing — before we wrap up, let me ask: what are you particularly good at or known for in your work, and what energizes you most about your role?

I'm known for my meticulous attention to detail and ability to streamline workflows. What energizes me most is seeing the tangible improvements in efficiency and knowing I'm making a difference in how smoothly things run.
That's a great strength — and how does knowledge sharing work across your teams, do you find that flows easily or are there gaps there?
Knowledge sharing generally flows well, but there are occasional gaps when teams are busy or priorities shift. We try to keep communication open to minimize those gaps.

I think we've now covered all the important topics — your role and responsibilities, your daily tasks with time estimates, the tools you use, your main frustrations and bottlenecks, and your clear ambitions for the future.

Thank you so much for taking the time to share all of this with me, Emily — it's been really valuable. You can now press the red button to end the conversation.
Alright, no problem.
